question: What is the primary objective of the School Health Programme?

options.A: Promoting and protecting the well-being of school-aged children
options.B: Regulating the curriculum of secondary schools nationwide
options.C: Replacing primary healthcare centers in rural communities
options.D: Providing academic scholarships for indigent students

explanation: The core mandate of any school health initiative centers on safeguarding the holistic health status of students while they acquire formal education. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why are schools considered strategic locations for public health interventions?

options.A: Teachers possess advanced clinical training in disease diagnosis
options.B: Children are legally required to receive vaccines at school only
options.C: Students spend a large portion of their formative years gathered in one place
options.D: Schools have larger budgets for medical equipment than hospitals

explanation: Concentrating large groups of children in a single institution allows public health programs to reach a wide demographic efficiently. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which activity is a primary responsibility of school health services?

options.A: Formulating national economic policies on education
options.B: Designing the architectural layout of school buildings
options.C: Conducting routine medical screenings for vision and hearing
options.D: Performing complex surgical procedures in the sick bay

explanation: Periodic physical assessments help catch sensory or growth deficits before they severely impact academic performance. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h2)

question: A student develops a sudden, severe asthma attack during physical education class. What is the most appropriate immediate action for the school nurse?

options.A: Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics to clear the airways
options.B: Provide first aid, administer prescribed rescue medication, and monitor closely
options.C: Send the child home unescorted to rest until the breathing normalizes
options.D: Wait until the end of the school day before notifying anyone

explanation: Acute episodes demand prompt emergency stabilization and rescue intervention right on site before considering further referral. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is a primary health risk associated with poor sanitation and lack of potable water in schools?

options.A: Congenital heart defects in newborn infants
options.C: Waterborne diseases such as cholera and typhoid
options.D: Chronic degenerative bone disorders in adolescents

explanation: Inadequate clean water and poor waste disposal directly facilitate the transmission of enteric pathogens among students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why must the psychosocial climate of a school be monitored as part of the health environment?

options.A: Mental health is unrelated to how students perform academically
options.B: Psychological stress causes immediate structural damage to school roofs
options.C: Emotional safety and freedom from bullying protect mental wellness
options.D: A positive mood replaces the need for standard physical health services

explanation: A safe psychological atmosphere prevents chronic stress, anxiety, and depression, ensuring learners thrive socially and cognitively. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of integrating health education into the school curriculum?

options.A: Transforming theoretical knowledge into lifelong healthy behaviors
options.B: Focusing exclusively on the anatomy of the skeletal system
options.C: Training every student to become a licensed medical doctor
options.D: Eliminating the need for practical physical education classes

explanation: Health education aims to equip students with practical habits that prevent disease and promote well-being throughout their lives. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which teaching method is generally most effective for engaging adolescents in health instruction?

options.A: Listening to uninterrupted lectures lasting several hours
options.B: Strict memorization of pharmacological drug dosages
options.C: Participatory methods like peer education and interactive discussions
options.D: Silent reading of dense medical textbooks without discussion

explanation: Active engagement and peer-led conversations resonate well with young people, encouraging open dialogue and behavior modification. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h4)

question: How does chronic malnutrition primarily impact a school-aged child?

options.A: It permanently enhances physical endurance and athletic speed
options.B: It eliminates the susceptibility to infectious disease outbreaks
options.C: It impairs cognitive development, concentration, and attendance
options.D: It accelerates the natural rate of bone density accumulation

explanation: Nutritional deficiencies rob the developing brain and body of essential fuel, directly translating to poor academic outcomes and frequent absences. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is a secondary benefit of well-managed school feeding programs beyond immediate nutrition?

options.A: Providing advanced training in surgical nursing procedures
options.B: Improving school attendance rates and boosting classroom engagement
options.C: Guaranteeing employment for students after graduation
options.D: Replacing the clinical responsibilities of local hospitals entirely

explanation: When children are assured of a meal at school, families are more motivated to send them consistently, reducing dropout rates. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which group acts as a vital bridge between the school system and local families for health mobilization?
explanation: PTAs facilitate communication and resource mobilization, ensuring that health policies initiated at school are understood and reinforced at home. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is the health and welfare of teachers specifically prioritized within the School Health Programme?

options.A: Teachers are legally classified as primary healthcare physicians
options.B: Staff members require more medical attention than students do
options.C: Educational policies forbid unwell individuals from entering classrooms
options.D: Healthy staff model positive behaviors and maintain a productive environment

explanation: Teachers who are physically and mentally well provide stable guidance and serve as powerful role models for impressionable learners. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary difference between monitoring and evaluation in a health program?

options.A: Monitoring tracks ongoing activities, while evaluation measures long-term impact
options.B: Monitoring is optional, while evaluation is strictly prohibited
options.C: Monitoring is performed by students, while evaluation is done by police
options.D: Monitoring focuses on finances, while evaluation focuses on architecture

explanation: Continuous tracking of daily processes constitutes monitoring, whereas assessing the ultimate outcomes and goals represents evaluation. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which metric is a direct indicator of a successful School Health Programme during evaluation?

options.A: Strict reduction in the number of active student clubs
options.B: Increased expenditure on architectural repairs for classrooms
options.C: Higher volume of administrative paperwork stored in offices
options.D: Reduction in student absenteeism due to preventable illnesses

explanation: Fewer sick days indicate that preventive services, nutrition, and environmental sanitation are effectively protecting student health. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h7)
